info.title: agentes.chat operator API
info.description: Workspace and account lookups, workspace standing, billing holds and limits (ADR 0079), the events feed and review blocks, the workspaces' computers from an external provisioner, who may sign up (the waiting list and early-access invitations, ADR 0078), how new Claude sign-ins for all agents are made (ADR 0150), and how connectors are used (ADR 0103), for the people who run this instance (ADR 0056).

state.description: `off` without both Turnstile keys. While `unreachable` (this server can't reach Cloudflare) or `secret_refused` (Cloudflare refuses `TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY`), every request goes through unchecked.

blocked.description: Networks refused in the last 10 minutes because their page couldn't load the check (`human_check_blocked`), each counted once: an IPv4 address, or an IPv6 /64. Any client can claim its page couldn't load it, so read it beside `passed`.

passed.description: Tokens Cloudflare passed in the last 10 minutes. When the widget is down for everyone, `blocked` rises while this falls. Clients claiming it is down don't move it.

testing.description: `TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY` is one of Cloudflare's test secrets. They refuse real tokens, and the one that passes takes a public dummy token from anyone. Right only on a test server.

OperatorBotCheck.description: The bot check before public forms (ADR 0075).

params.description: Values for the translated message (names, limits…).

next.description: `cursor` for the next page; null on the last one.

OperatorStandingState.description: `active`; `hold`: its agents stop (no model, computer, routine or invitation), people still read and write; `suspended`: the workspace refuses everything to everyone, and its runs and tasks stop at once.

lastSeenAt.description: Last time they had this workspace open.

channels.description: Channels, not archived; no direct messages.

dueAt.description: When it is deleted for good, unless a hold keeps it longer.

requestedBy.description: Who asked; null once their account is gone.

deletion.description: Its deletion, asked by an owner or with its only member's account: closed until `dueAt`. Null when it isn't being deleted.

deletionHold.description: The operator's deletion hold (`PUT /orgs/{orgId}/deletion-hold`); null when none.

note.description: The operator's own note: never shown to the workspace.

OperatorStandingNotice.description: `shown`: the workspace is told the reason, the change goes into its audit log and a new state notifies its owners and admins. `silent`: it is told only that it is paused, and nothing is written where it can read it. Use `silent` only when an authority's order forbids telling them.

updatedAt.description: When a value last changed; null: never set.

OperatorLimitsState.description: Null: no limit. A self-hosted server never sets any.

members.description: People in it, blocked accounts included; agents, invitations and requests to join never count.

membersMax.description: The most people its plan takes with seats added. Below it, the apps tell whoever manages billing that a full workspace can add a seat; at it, that the plan can change. Null (or left out): not said, and the apps say neither.

payerUserId.description: The user id of whoever pays for its plan, the only one who can add seats or change plans. In a full workspace they read that they can add a seat, and anyone else who manages billing reads to ask them, by name while they are in the workspace. Null (or left out): not said, and whoever manages billing reads that they can add a seat.

uploadBytesPerDay.description: Bytes written to this server's storage in any 24 hours.

platformUsdPerMonth.description: What the platform's own AI (Jev) may cost for it in a UTC calendar month, in US$. Past it, Jev's judgments go to the workspace's own model and only @mentions start agents.

standby.description: You put the workspace's computer in standby (`PUT …/standby`) and it hasn't connected since. False for every other computer.

busy.description: The workspace's computer is in use now: a run of the workspace queued or running, a run waiting for this computer, a task running on it, someone in control of one of its agents' screens, or someone wanting it in the last 2 minutes (an open view of it asks every few seconds). Busy in standby: something waits for it. False for every other computer.

One account: its workspaces and newest sessions

put.summary: Hold, suspend or restore a workspace
put.description: Enforced by this server where work starts: model calls, computer calls, routines, invitations and, when suspended, every permission check. Suspending also stops its runs and its tasks on computers now; cutting a computer's network is up to the operator's own controls on it. Held or suspended, it waits for no computer: what its provisioner last said goes (a ready computer stays), and it is a request again once active. It takes effect at once in this process and within 5 seconds in the server's others. Setting what is already set tells nobody again.

reason.description: Shown to the workspace with the notice `shown`, its owners' notice included. On agentes.chat Cloud, `review` reads as the automatic review hold's line, `review.<category>` as that line naming what was flagged (`phishing_impersonation`, `account_takeover`, `fraud` or `illegal_content`, any other category reading as plain `review`), `ended` (a plan that ended) as it is, and any other reason is followed by how to contest it, so name the Terms section it rests on.

put.summary: Hold one agent, or let it go
put.description: Held, the agent starts nothing (no run, model call, computer work, routine or bridge call) and is never picked to answer; the rest of the workspace works. What it is doing stops at its next model, computer or bridge call. The workspace reads only that the agent is paused, never the reason. On agentes.chat Cloud it reads the hold's kind with how to contest it (`network` for a reason starting with `network.`, else `operator`), and the agent's responsible person and the workspace's owners and admins get a notice, replaced when it is held again for another kind and closed when the agent is let go. At once in this process, within 5 seconds in the others.

put.summary: Hold a workspace's deletion (a legal hold), or let it go
put.description: While held, a workspace whose deletion was asked for (by an owner, or with its only member's account) waits past its date instead of being deleted: it stays closed, with everything in it. Nothing is refused and the workspace is told nothing: no audit row, no notice. Restoring the workspace never lifts it. Let go, a deletion past its date goes ahead within an hour.

put.summary: Block an account, or let it back
put.description: Blocked: its sessions and phones are signed out now, it can't sign in again, every workspace refuses it on its next request (no waiting for a session cookie to expire) and its open connections close. Unblocking lets it sign in again; it keeps its workspaces. On agentes.chat Cloud the refused sign-in reads the block's kind, never its reason: `abuse` for `abuse.resignup`, `legal` for `legal_hold`, else `other`.

put.summary: Put a billing hold on a workspace, change its code, or lift it
put.description: A billing hold is a hold with one of these codes as its reason and the notice `shown`: the workspace reads it in its own words, and owners and admins get the way to fix it. It never replaces nor lifts a hold set through PUT /standing or a suspension (`applied: false`); one of those replaces it, so set it again once that is lifted. Its owners and admins are notified when the state changes.

All at once. Enforced where each is used: joining and inviting (`org.members_full`), every file written to this server's storage (`storage.full`, `storage.daily_full`), the platform's AI (within a minute). Lowering one takes nothing away: people stay, files stay, only what is new is refused. Allowed whatever the workspace's standing. Setting what is already set changes nothing, `updatedAt` included.

get.description: Active workspaces whose computer isn't ready (one on hold, suspended or being deleted is never listed). Empty unless `MACHINE_PROVISIONING=external`.

put.summary: Say how far the workspace's computer is
put.description: Its people see it live, with the time left and the stage. The time `since` restarts only when the state, step or reason change. One wait counts down to the earliest ready time you gave it: a later one changes nothing they see, so a part running long reads as running over, until another state, a removal or a hold starts a new wait. A ready time over a minute ahead (the wait's earliest), `waiting` or `problem` tells the owners they'll get an email when it's ready (when this server sends email). Refused (409 `provisioning.ready`) once the computer is ready, until it is removed, and (403 `org.paused`, `org.suspended`, `org.deleting`) unless the workspace is active and not being deleted: one held, suspended or being deleted waits for no computer, and what you last said of it is gone.

state.description: `ready` is not yours to set: it comes with the computer's first hello.

step.description: With `preparing`: reserving, starting, installing or connecting; ignored otherwise.

stage.description: With `preparing`: what the computer is doing within `step` (ordering, wiping, starting, booting, updating, restarting, network, firewall, apps, connecting); ignored otherwise. Any word is kept: the apps say one they have no words for as its step.

reason.description: With `waiting`: capacity; ignored otherwise. `approval`, from an older client, reads as capacity.

expectedReadyAt.description: With `preparing`: when the computer should be ready, at most 7 days ahead; ignored otherwise. A wait counts down to the earliest time it was told: a later one, or a report without one, leaves it as it is, so people see the wait run over.

etaSeconds.description: From an older client, in place of `expectedReadyAt`: read as that many seconds from now.

post.summary: The workspace's computer, and a code for it to connect with
post.description: One per workspace: the first call makes it, every later one issues a new code for the same computer (an earlier unused code stops working), and one removed comes back. The code lives 10 minutes; once redeemed, the computer's first hello makes it ready and gives it the workspace's agents that have no computer. Refused (403 `org.paused`, `org.suspended`, `org.deleting`) unless the workspace is active and not being deleted.

get.summary: The workspace's computers, its own and the ones its people connected

put.summary: Say the workspace's computer is in standby, or no longer
put.description: Say it when you put the computer to sleep (`true`), or that it no longer is (`false`; its first hello clears it too). In standby nothing is wrong to its people: it opens as it wakes, and it is never listed as disconnected. Whatever wants it meanwhile (a run, a person opening it, a request to it) records `machine.wake_wanted` in the events feed, at most every 10 seconds per computer: wake it then. A run waits up to a minute for it before it tells its people the computer isn't answering. `true` again keeps the first time it was said. 404 when the workspace has no such managed computer.

put.summary: Say the workspace's computer's agents wait for their way out, or no longer
put.description: Say it (`true`) when the computer's network sends its agents out only through a proxy and none works now, so their connections are refused for a while; `false` once one works. Its people see a line saying so on the computer, never an error, while it is online. `true` again keeps the first time it was said; removing the computer ends it. A change comes as `machine.updated`. 404 when the workspace has no such managed computer.

delete.description: Before wiping or retiring it: its token and unused codes stop working, its connection closes, its agents are left with no computer, and an active workspace is a request again, waiting from now (one held or suspended waits for none). 404 when the workspace has no such managed computer (also when it was already removed).

put.description: Takes effect at once, with no restart. Setting the current mode changes nothing. On agentes.chat Cloud, while it is `invite`, only the accounts early access allowed make workspaces, as many as they like; `open` lets every account make workspaces, each with its own computer. Refused (409 `signup.host_computer`) to open while this server is its agents' computer (`HOST_COMPUTER_TOKEN`).

409.description: This server is its agents' computer (`signup.host_computer`)

get.summary: The waiting list against the invitations
The next confirmed entries still waiting, oldest first
get.description: A read: invite exactly these (`POST /early-access/invitations`), so a retry never invites more than you saw. An address with an account is among them: inviting it allows the account. Skips addresses sign-up wouldn't take and those of blocked accounts; they still count as waiting.

post.summary: Add confirmed addresses to the waiting list
post.description: In one transaction, up to 5000 entries, deduplicated on the address in lower case. New ones join confirmed, at `joinedAt` (a future one reads as now) or else in the list's order; an unconfirmed entry is confirmed; anything else is `unchanged`, so a repeat changes nothing. `invalid` holds the indexes of the entries that aren't addresses (sign-up's own rule), never the addresses. Imported entries are never sent to the email provider's contacts.

post.summary: Invite addresses to create an account and make workspaces
post.description: Each address, up to 200, gets an email with a link to sign up with that address only, valid 14 days, in the language of its invitation, else of its waiting-list entry, else `locale`, else English. An address that has an account gets no link: the account is allowed at once, and an email in its language says so (none to a blocked account). An allowed account makes workspaces once its address is confirmed. One invitation per address: inviting it again sends the same invitation a new link (the old one stops working), unless `resend` is false. Answers come in the request's order, once per address. Outcomes: `invalid_email`, `signed_up` (its invitation made an account or allowed one already, so nothing went out), `allowed`, `already_invited` (with `resend: false`), `recent` (sent in the last 2 minutes, so nothing went out), `resent`, `invited`. Refused (409 `early_access.no_email`) on a server that sends no email.

post.summary: Send an invitation again, with a new link
post.description: The old link stops working, the invitation is no longer revoked and runs 14 days from now. Within 2 minutes of the previous send nothing goes out (`sent: false`). When the address has an account by now, no link goes: the account is allowed at once and an email says so (none to a blocked account), and the answer is the invitation, now `signed_up`, with `sent: false`. Refused (409) once it was used (`early_access.used`), and on a server that sends no email (`early_access.no_email`).
Its link stops working, and its account can make no more workspaces while sign-up is by invitation. The workspaces it made stay. Revoking again answers the same.
